PairingMethod.description: Which representation of a pairing challenge the device presents.

oneOf.description: The high-entropy credential carried by the QR payload.
The short code typed by hand next to the address.

Secret.description:
A pairing credential, manual code or device token. Serializes as a plain
string; `Debug` never prints the value, so it cannot reach logs or error
strings through a derived impl.

description: First frame from a device. Anything else closes the connection.

oneOf.description:
Ask the host's owner to let this device pair. Carries no secret. The
socket stays open for the answer (`connect_pending`, then
`connect_approved`, `connect_denied` or `connect_expired`); after
`connect_approved` it sends one `pair` frame with `method: "code"` and
the code the owner reads off the host. Only gateways that list
`connect_requests` in their Bonjour `caps` take it.

device_kind.description:
As in `pair`. Recorded with the device when it pairs, over
whatever its `pair` frame says, because it is what the owner saw.

device_name.description: A label chosen by the device, shown to the owner. Never an identity.

install_id.description:
As in `pair`. A new request from the same address and install
replaces the one still open, so a reconnecting app does not wait
for its old request to expire.

platform.description:
What the device runs on, for the owner: `ios`, `android`,
`macos`, `windows`, `linux`, ….

oneOf.description: Exchange a pairing challenge for a device token.

device_kind.description:
What the device is: `phone`, `desktop` (the desktop app on
another machine) or `cli`. Absent, or a kind this gateway does
not know, is a phone. A label for the owner, not a permission.
Gateways that list `desktops` record it; it never grants ACP access.

device_name.description: A label chosen by the device. Never an identity.

host_id.description:
The stable identifier of the machine a desktop app or command
line runs on, which the owner may pair with in turn. Ignored
unless it is 16 to 128 printable ASCII characters.

install_id.description:
A random identifier the app generates once per install and keeps.
Pairing again with the same one replaces that install's earlier
device record and revokes its token, instead of adding a record.
Not tied to the user; ignored unless it is 16 to 128 printable
ASCII characters. Older apps leave it out.

platform.description:
What the device runs on: `ios`, `android`, `macos`, `windows`,
`linux`, …. Absent is `unknown`.

wire_names.description: `"thread"` asks for the thread names on the wire; see [`WIRE_NAMES_THREAD`].

oneOf.description: Present a device token obtained from an earlier `paired` frame.

wire_names.description: `"thread"` asks for the thread names on the wire; see [`WIRE_NAMES_THREAD`].
